# Handoff: project state as of Nov 21, 2026

Read this first in a new chat, then `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/BACKLOG.md` and `docs/IDEAS.md`. It records everything
decided and built across the long build session, so no context is lost.

## Where things stand
- **Branch:** `claude/file-editing-offline-9q9lv2` holds all work. PR #1 (everything up to the 3D campus) was merged
  into `main`. Everything after it is on the branch only, and needs a **new PR** to reach `main` (Vercel deploys from
  `main`). That covers the polish passes, the explored campus, day/night models, onboarding, the legend and these docs.
- **Ryan's laptop changes are not on GitHub yet.** Suggested flow: push them to a `laptop-work` branch, then merge it
  with this branch and resolve conflicts. Both branches touch the UI.
- **Backlog:** every item is done. The remaining work is the **UI polish plan** in `docs/BACKLOG.md` (typography,
  motion, accessibility, cover art) and the ideas awaiting approval in `docs/IDEAS.md` (§0 ranks them by hackathon win odds).

## What's built (one spec per feature in `specs/`)
| Spec | Feature |
|---|---|
| 001–009 | Foundation, missions/profiles, friends + building cards, replay, rank + badges, neighbourhoods, ping log, leaderboards, time-of-day lighting |
| 010 | The Goose quest-giver: original SVG portrait; Gemini re-voices briefings with a fact guard |
| 011 | Geo-pinned tags: server gate on revealed cells; upvotes give +10 Rep; local/demo mode |
| 012 | 11 sourced London landmark missions, map-menu overview, region tap raise, cinematic intro, brand emblem |
| 013 | Forest FM radio: facts-only scripts, Gemini TTS or the browser's speech voice, captions |
| 014 | Graduation Wrapped: story slides, fog timelapse, real stats, share card |
| 015 | Live LTC buses (GTFS + GTFS-RT), next arrivals, ride detection, Every Route badge |
| 016 | Faculty turf + 3-player heists |
| 017 | Polish pack: collectibles, radar, posters, fog decay, weather, student-written missions |
| 018 | Class Run: private schedule, next-class waypoints, on-time Rep |
| 019 | Hand-built 3D campus models (glTF via script) |
| 020 | Mustang City always explored inside Western's real boundary, sharp border, all 160 campus buildings modelled |

UI polish passes (commits after 019) changed the following:
- **Look:** soft rounded glass with no cut corners, sunset pill buttons, and the golden-hour palette.
- **Fog:** Chaikin-smoothed edges with a feathered rim.
- **Map:** one control stack, building framing on tap, and a postcard loading screen built from renders of our own campus.
- **Models and art:** day/night model variants and the soft Wrapped art.
- **New players:** onboarding cards and a map legend with layer toggles.

## Decisions to keep
- **Original IP only:** no GTA/Rockstar names, logos, fonts or art. Public copy may only say "GTA 6-inspired". No parody
  of the GTA logo; the cover-art collage uses our own wordmark (`docs/COVER_ART.md`).
- **Accuracy rule:** landmark, collectible and radio facts come from stored, sourced text. Gemini may restyle text but
  never adds facts, and numbers are guard-checked.
- **Mustang City cells** are always revealed but never count toward Rep, % explored, districts, leaderboards or sync.
- **Fog decay** is a haze only: explored ground never un-explores.
- **Privacy:** no live location sharing; the Class Run schedule stays on the device; loot challenges (an idea, not built)
  must be opt-in with coarse areas only.
- **Database:** keep Tiger Data (TimescaleDB hypertable + continuous aggregate, MLH prize). Supabase is recommended as
  an add-on for Realtime and Storage only, because Supabase dropped TimescaleDB on Postgres 17 (`docs/SETUP_KEYS.md`).
- **Turf** uses cleared cells per faculty, not Rep, because cells are what's geographic.
- **Design direction:** a clean, soft, premium mobile app. GTA 6 flavour comes from the art direction (postcards, sunset
  palette, full-bleed loading art, establishing-shot captions), not from hard or polygonal shapes.
- Push only to the `claude/...` branch unless Ryan says otherwise. Force-push was blocked once, so merge instead.

## Needs from Ryan (also `docs/IDEAS.md` §7 and `docs/SETUP_KEYS.md`)
- **Keys:** `GEMINI_API_KEY`, the Auth0 settings and `DATABASE_URL`, then run `npm run db:schema && npm run db:seed`.
  The schema has new tables and columns since the last seed: `tag_votes`, `missions.created_at` and the heist index.
- **Deploy:** a new PR from this branch into `main`.
- **Optional:** comic-panel art and icon (prompts in `docs/COVER_ART.md`).
- **Checks on the deployed site:** live LTC buses (the realtime host reset connections from the cloud build machine)
  and Open-Meteo weather (it returned 429 to the cloud machine).

## Running locally
- `.env.local` needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` (a public `pk.` token; allow localhost in its URL restrictions).
  `LTC_FIXTURE=1` simulates buses in dev only.
- `npm run dev`. Press **D** for demo controls: walk campus, reveal here, light presets, weather, fog ageing, sample turf,
  demo heist crew, replay intro.
- **Regenerate data:**
  - `npm run gtfs:build <unzipped LTC GTFS dir>` → `lib/data/ltc.json`
  - `npm run models:extract <dir of Mapbox Streets z15 tiles>` → `scripts/models/campus-all.json`
  - `npm run models:build` → `public/models/*.glb` (night and `-day` variants) + `lib/data/campusModels.json`
- **Cloud sessions:** the `mustang-city` cloud environment allows `api.mapbox.com`, `events.mapbox.com`,
  `gtfs.ltconline.ca`, `www.londontransit.ca` and `api.open-meteo.com`.

## Gotchas learned the hard way
- **Mapbox glTF:** vertex buffers must not be interleaved (`VertexLayout.SEPARATE`), indices must be uint16, and
  `addModel` needs absolute URLs. Axes: +X east, +Y up, +Z south. A `clip` layer needs `clip-layer-scope: ["basemap"]`,
  or it hides our own models whose anchor sits inside the clip polygon.
- **Material glow** ignores the layer's `model-emissive-strength`. That's why there are separate `-day` model files.
- **Next 16 with `cacheComponents`:** a route handler that doesn't read the request gets prerendered. Call `await connection()`.
- **The dev server sometimes serves stale CSS** after edits in this container. Restart `next dev` if styles don't change.
- **Tile-split buildings:** Mapbox vector tiles split buildings at tile edges. Footprint matching must test vertex
  overlap both ways (see `replacedByModel` in `MapView.tsx`).
- **Headless browser screenshots:** use `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader`. Run the scripts from the scratchpad,
  not the repo root, or the screenshots land in git.

## Ideas logged but not built (see `docs/IDEAS.md`)
- **Ranked list (§0):** Devpost trailer, comic-panel cover intro, live big-screen mirror, "wanted level" stars, The Goose
  calls you, the stash and carry inventory (Mustang City as the stash), loot challenges as a London trivia duel, pause
  music, photo mode and more.
- **3D models (§3):** phone photogrammetry is the upgrade path to photo-real facades.
- **Pause music (§4):** procedural, licensed or AI-generated routes.

# Mustang City — pitch & demo script

> **One line:** Most Western students spend four years in London and leave knowing only campus, Richmond Row and the 2 bus.
> Mustang City turns London into an open world you uncover — so you graduate knowing your city, and leave with memories of it.

## The story (say it like this)

1. **The problem (personal):** "Most of us didn't grow up here. We arrive at 18, live inside a bubble — campus, Richmond Row,
   one bus route — and four years later we leave. *Almost 85% of Western students leave London after they graduate.*\*
   Most will never come back. We spend four years in a city and never actually meet it."
2. **The insight:** "We already explore cities obsessively — in games. Open-world games make you *want* to see what's behind
   the fog. So what if London *was* the open world?"
3. **The product:** "Mustang City covers London in black fog. It only clears where you've physically walked. Western is your
   home base — Mustang City — and everything else is Forest State, waiting."
4. **Why you'd go:** "The Goose — our crime-boss quest-giver — sends you on missions to real places with real history:
   the house where insulin was conceived, the street that played 1980s New York for Apple TV. A photo proves you went;
   Gemini checks it. You earn Rep, unlock neighbourhoods, ride real LTC buses, and pull heists with people you just met."
5. **What you leave with:** "At graduation you get your Wrapped: the fog you cleared in the order you cleared it, the places,
   the photos, the people. Not just a degree — a map of your four years in London."
6. **Close:** "Graduate knowing your city."

\* Quote from Amir Farahi (London Institute) via 106.9 The X — **verify the exact figure before saying it on stage**; if unsure,
say "the vast majority". International students are ~24% of Western (Times Higher Education).

## Wow features — in priority order

Rank = (how much a judge notices it) × (how reliably it works on stage). Build/practice in this order.

| # | Moment | Why it lands | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cinematic intro flight** (title card → letterboxed dive from Forest State into Mustang City) | First 15 seconds; instantly reads as "open-world game" | ✅ built |
| 2 | **Fog clearing timelapse** (Replay of a real walk at 16–48×) | The one image that explains the product | ✅ built — **record your real Saturday walk** |
| 3 | **3D Mustang City** (hand-built Middlesex tower, UC, 160 campus buildings, tap → history card) | Craft + "this is our campus" | ✅ built |
| 4 | **Mission → Gemini photo check → MISSION PASSED** | The game loop + sponsor tech in one beat | ⚠️ needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` (check-in missions work now) |
| 5 | **Live LTC buses** on the map + "Route 2 in 4 min" on a mission card | Real-time data; judges love "that's live" | ✅ working (114 live buses) |
| 6 | **Wrapped share card** — "Graduate knowing your city" | Emotional close: the memory you leave with | ✅ built |
| 7 | Neighbourhood unlock + "Entering East London" banner | Shows the city opening up | ✅ built |
| 8 | Crew compare + faculty turf + heist | Social pitch: meeting people | ✅ built — real accounts need Auth0 + DB |
| 9 | Forest FM radio host | Personality; Gemini TTS voice | ✅ built — Gemini voice needs key |
| 10 | Geo-pinned tags ("left by whoever came before you") | Memories left *for* others | ✅ built |

**Highest-leverage things still to do before judging:** (1) add the Gemini key and test a photo mission end to end,
(2) record one real campus walk for Replay, (3) drop in the cover art, (4) rehearse the script below 3×.

## Demo scripts

Use the **laptop phone frame** (judges see exactly the phone UI). Press **D** for the hidden demo panel. Have the iPhone
(home-screen icon) as backup and a recorded video as the last resort.

### 60 seconds (expo table / fly-by)
1. (0–10 s) Title card → **Tap to enter** → intro flight. *"Most Western students leave London never having seen it."*
2. (10–25 s) Demo panel → **Replay sample walk (48×)** — fog clears across campus. *"The fog only clears where you've walked."*
3. (25–40 s) Tap Middlesex College → history card. *"Every building has a story."*
4. (40–60 s) Profile → **Forest State Wrapped** → share card. *"Graduate knowing your city."*

### 3 minutes (main judging)
| Time | Beat | Do | Say |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Hook | Title card on screen | Story points 1–2 |
| 0:20–0:40 | Intro | Tap to enter → flight | "London becomes Forest State. Western is Mustang City — home base." |
| 0:40–1:05 | Fog | Demo panel → Replay your real walk (16×), then zoom out to city view | "Black fog everywhere you haven't been. % explored, neighbourhoods unlock at 30%." |
| 1:05–1:25 | 3D campus | Fly to Mustang City, tilt, tap Middlesex | "Hand-built 3D campus. Tap any building for its real history." |
| 1:25–2:05 | Mission | Missions → Banting House (or Meet The Family) → Goose briefing → Teleport (demo) → photo → **MISSION PASSED** | "The Goose sends you to real places. Gemini checks your photo. You earn Rep." |
| 2:05–2:25 | Live city | Zoom to downtown: live buses; open a mission card: "Route 2 in 4 min" | "That's live London Transit — missions tell you which bus gets you there." |
| 2:25–2:45 | Social | Crew → compare with a friend, show their fog; mention turf + heists | "Faculties fight over neighbourhoods. Heists need three people at once — strangers meet." |
| 2:45–3:00 | Close | Profile → Wrapped → share card | Story points 5–6: "Graduate knowing your city." |

### 5 minutes (if you get it)
Add after 2:45: Forest FM radio segment (15 s) · leave a tag (20 s) · "Entering East London" banner via demo walk (Old East Village is inside it) (20 s) ·
tech slide: Next.js PWA, Mapbox Standard + hand-built glTF, H3 fog, Gemini (vision + TTS + guarded rewrites),
Auth0 @uwo.ca Action, Tiger Data hypertable + continuous aggregate, live GTFS-RT (45 s).

## Before you walk up (checklist)
- [ ] Laptop: app open, intro **not yet seen this session** (so the flight plays), demo panel tested, light preset = Dusk
- [ ] Sound on (MISSION PASSED sting, radio) — but low
- [ ] Phone: home-screen icon, logged in, location on, battery > 50%
- [ ] Real Replay walk recorded; a real mission photo on the laptop for the photo picker
- [ ] Projector check: text readable at the frame's scaled size
- [ ] Backup video on the desktop

## Likely questions (additions to the brief's Q&A)
- **"Why would students keep using it after week one?"** Fog slowly hazes over (come back), weekly turf, new student missions,
  Class Run turns your daily commute into Rep, and Wrapped rewards the whole four years.
- **"What about students who never leave campus?"** Missions start at the campus edge and use buses — the app literally tells
  you which bus to take next.
- **"Does the city benefit?"** Students who know the city are more likely to stay after graduation; local businesses can sponsor missions.
- **"Is location safe?"** No live location sharing. Friends only see *where* you've been (cleared fog), never *when* or where you are.

Sources: [106.9 The X (London Institute quote)](https://www.1069thex.com/?p=24964) ·
[Times Higher Education — Western](https://resouces-cms.prd.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/western-university)
# Mustang City — Product Brief

# Mustang City — pitch & demo script

> **One line:** Most Western students spend four years in London and leave knowing only campus, Richmond Row and the 2 bus.
> Mustang City turns London into an open world you uncover — so you graduate knowing your city, and leave with memories of it.

## The story (say it like this)

1. **The problem (personal):** "Most of us didn't grow up here. We arrive at 18, live inside a bubble — campus, Richmond Row,
   one bus route — and four years later we leave. *Almost 85% of Western students leave London after they graduate.*\*
   Most will never come back. We spend four years in a city and never actually meet it."
2. **The insight:** "We already explore cities obsessively — in games. Open-world games make you *want* to see what's behind
   the fog. So what if London *was* the open world?"
3. **The product:** "Mustang City covers London in black fog. It only clears where you've physically walked. Western is your
   home base — Mustang City — and everything else is Forest State, waiting."
4. **Why you'd go:** "The Goose — our crime-boss quest-giver — sends you on missions to real places with real history:
   the house where insulin was conceived, the street that played 1980s New York for Apple TV. A photo proves you went;
   Gemini checks it. You earn Rep, unlock neighbourhoods, ride real LTC buses, and pull heists with people you just met."
5. **What you leave with:** "At graduation you get your Wrapped: the fog you cleared in the order you cleared it, the places,
   the photos, the people. Not just a degree — a map of your four years in London."
6. **Close:** "Graduate knowing your city."

\* Quote from Amir Farahi (London Institute) via 106.9 The X — **verify the exact figure before saying it on stage**; if unsure,
say "the vast majority". International students are ~24% of Western (Times Higher Education).

## Wow features — in priority order

Rank = (how much a judge notices it) × (how reliably it works on stage). Build/practice in this order.

| # | Moment | Why it lands | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cinematic intro flight** (title card → letterboxed dive from Forest State into Mustang City) | First 15 seconds; instantly reads as "open-world game" | ✅ built |
| 2 | **Fog clearing timelapse** (Replay of a real walk at 16–48×) | The one image that explains the product | ✅ built — **record your real Saturday walk** |
| 3 | **3D Mustang City** (hand-built Middlesex tower, UC, 160 campus buildings, tap → history card) | Craft + "this is our campus" | ✅ built |
| 4 | **Mission → Gemini photo check → MISSION PASSED** | The game loop + sponsor tech in one beat | ⚠️ needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` (check-in missions work now) |
| 5 | **Live LTC buses** on the map + "Route 2 in 4 min" on a mission card | Real-time data; judges love "that's live" | ✅ working (114 live buses) |
| 6 | **Wrapped share card** — "Graduate knowing your city" | Emotional close: the memory you leave with | ✅ built |
| 7 | Neighbourhood unlock + "Entering East London" banner | Shows the city opening up | ✅ built |
| 8 | Crew compare + faculty turf + heist | Social pitch: meeting people | ✅ built — real accounts need Auth0 + DB |
| 9 | Forest FM radio host | Personality; Gemini TTS voice | ✅ built — Gemini voice needs key |
| 10 | Geo-pinned tags ("left by whoever came before you") | Memories left *for* others | ✅ built |

3. (25–40 s) Tap Middlesex College → history card. *"Every building has a story."*
4. (40–60 s) Profile → **Forest State Wrapped** → share card. *"Graduate knowing your city."*

|---|---|---|---|

| 0:40–1:05 | Fog | Demo panel → Replay your real walk (16×), then zoom out to city view | "Black fog everywhere you haven't been. % explored, neighbourhoods unlock at 30%." |

| 1:25–2:05 | Mission | Missions → Banting House (or Meet The Family) → Goose briefing → Teleport (demo) → photo → **MISSION PASSED** | "The Goose sends you to real places. Gemini checks your photo. You earn Rep." |

| 2:45–3:00 | Close | Profile → Wrapped → share card | Story points 5–6: "Graduate knowing your city." |

Add after 2:45: Forest FM radio segment (15 s) · leave a tag (20 s) · "Entering East London" banner via demo walk (Old East Village is inside it) (20 s) ·

- [ ] Laptop: app open, intro **not yet seen this session** (so the flight plays), demo panel tested, light preset = Dusk
- [ ] Sound on (MISSION PASSED sting, radio) — but low
- [ ] Phone: home-screen icon, logged in, location on, battery > 50%
- [ ] Real Replay walk recorded; a real mission photo on the laptop for the photo picker
- [ ] Projector check: text readable at the frame's scaled size
- [ ] Backup video on the desktop

## Likely questions (additions to the brief's Q&A)
- **"Why would students keep using it after week one?"** Fog slowly hazes over (come back), weekly turf, new student missions,
  Class Run turns your daily commute into Rep, and Wrapped rewards the whole four years.
- **"What about students who never leave campus?"** Missions start at the campus edge and use buses — the app literally tells
  you which bus to take next.
- **"Does the city benefit?"** Students who know the city are more likely to stay after graduation; local businesses can sponsor missions.
- **"Is location safe?"** No live location sharing. Friends only see *where* you've been (cleared fog), never *when* or where you are.

Here's everything for the Devpost form. I pulled it from your handoff, pitch and brief docs, and there are no em dashes in any of it.

---

## About the project (paste into Project Story)

```markdown
## Inspiration

Most of us didn't grow up in London. We arrive at 18, live inside a bubble of campus, Richmond Row and one bus route, and four years later the vast majority of us leave. We spend four years in a city and never actually meet it.

We already explore cities obsessively, just in games. Open-world games make you *want* to see what's behind the fog. So I asked: what if London was the open world?

## What it does

**Mustang City** is a GTA 6-inspired mobile web app that turns London, Ontario into **Forest State**, an open-world map covered in black fog. The fog only clears where you've physically walked. Western's campus is your home base, Mustang City, and everything else is waiting to be uncovered.

- **Fog of war:** your real GPS path clears the map, cell by cell, with smoothed, feathered edges.
- **3D Mustang City:** all 160 campus buildings are modelled in 3D, with day and night versions. Tap any building for its real history.
- **Photo missions:** The Goose, an original crime-boss quest-giver, sends you to real places with real history, like the house where insulin was conceived. Snap a photo to prove you went, and Gemini checks it. Then: **MISSION PASSED**.
- **Rep, ranks and neighbourhoods:** earn Rep, unlock badges, and watch "Entering Old East Village" banners as the city opens up.
- **Live LTC buses:** real-time buses on the map, plus "Route 2 in 4 min" right on your mission card. The app detects bus rides too.
- **Social:** compare fog with friends, fight for neighbourhoods by faculty, and pull three-player heists that get strangers to meet.
- **Forest FM:** an in-game radio host that reads facts-only scripts in a Gemini TTS voice.
- **Geo-pinned tags:** leave notes on places for whoever comes after you.
- **Class Run:** your daily walk to class earns Rep for being on time. Your schedule never leaves your phone.
- **Graduation Wrapped:** a story-style recap of the fog you cleared, in the order you cleared it, with the places and the people. Not just a degree, but a map of your four years in London.

**Graduate knowing your city.**

## How I built it

- **Frontend:** Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind v4 and Motion, shipped as a PWA for the iPhone home screen. On a laptop it renders inside a phone frame.
- **Map:** one Mapbox GL JS instance on the Standard style. The fog is an H3 hex grid merged into a single polygon and smoothed with Chaikin's algorithm.
- **3D campus:** I wrote a script that turns building footprints into glTF models, with separate day and night files because Mapbox ignores emissive strength on material glow.
- **AI:** Gemini handles photo verification, mission briefings in The Goose's voice, and radio TTS. A strict rule covers all of it: facts come from stored, sourced text. Gemini may restyle a sentence but never add a fact, and a guard checks every number.
- **Transit:** LTC's static GTFS is preprocessed into a compact dataset, and the live bus positions and arrivals come from GTFS-Realtime.
- **Auth and data:** Auth0 with a post-login Action that only allows @uwo.ca accounts. Data lives in Tiger Data (Postgres + TimescaleDB): location pings go into a hypertable with a continuous aggregate for leaderboards.
- **Hosting:** Vercel. Weather comes from Open-Meteo.
- **Process:** I built this solo with AI coding agents, writing a spec for each of 20 features before building it.

## Challenges

- **Getting custom 3D models into Mapbox:** I found out the hard way that vertex buffers can't be interleaved, indices must be uint16, and model URLs must be absolute. Clip layers also hid my own models until I scoped them to the basemap.
- **Buildings split at tile edges:** Mapbox vector tiles cut buildings at tile boundaries, so matching footprints to my models meant testing vertex overlap both ways.
- **Fog that looks good:** raw hexagons look like a spreadsheet. Merging, smoothing and feathering them took several passes.
- **Live transit from the cloud:** the LTC realtime server reset TLS connections from the build machine, so I added an HTTP fallback.
- **Accuracy vs. personality:** I wanted The Goose to be funny without making up history. That's why the fact guard exists.
- **Privacy:** there's no live location sharing. Friends only see *where* you've been (cleared fog), never *when*, and never where you are right now.

## What I learned

- How to bend a map engine into a game engine: fog, a HUD, mission flow and a cinematic intro camera.
- How to generate 3D glTF from scratch, and how to work with GTFS and GTFS-Realtime.
- How to design around time-series data with TimescaleDB hypertables.
- How to keep an LLM useful without letting it make things up.
- How to scope ruthlessly as a solo builder: one strong image (fog clearing as you walk) beats ten half-finished features.

## What's next

Phone photogrammetry for photo-real campus facades, student-written missions at scale, and local businesses sponsoring missions to get students off campus and into the city.
```

---

## Built with (25 tags, the maximum)

```
next.js, typescript, react, tailwind-css, motion, mapbox, mapbox-gl-js, h3, gltf, auth0, tiger-data, timescaledb, postgresql, gemini, google-gemini, gtfs, gtfs-realtime, open-meteo, vercel, pwa, node.js, javascript, web-speech-api, claude-code, spec-kit
```

---

## "Try it out" links

- **Code:** https://github.com/RyanPeters06/mustang-city
- **Live app:** your Vercel URL (I don't have it, so add it yourself)

---

A few things to check before you submit:
- **Make the repo public** if it's private, or the Code link won't work for judges.
- **Photo missions say Gemini checks the photo.** That only works once `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set on Vercel, and the handoff says it hasn't been tested end to end yet. If you don't get to it, soften that line.
- **Heists, the faculty turf fight and comparing fog with friends** need real accounts, so Auth0 and the database have to be live on the deployed site.
- **Adjust "20 features"** if your count of specs is different.

content.content:
# Cover art + app icon: generation guide

Goal: a fragmented comic-panel collage (the classic open-world game cover layout), all London, Ontario themed,
for the intro title card, Devpost thumbnail and app icon. **Original art only**: no GTA/Rockstar names, logo,
typeface or characters; no copying of existing covers. The *layout style* is generic and fine.

## Rules for every prompt
- Never write "GTA", "Grand Theft Auto", "Rockstar" or "Vice City" in a prompt, and never upload an existing game cover as
  a reference image (image-to-image would copy it).
- No text or logos in the images. The Mustang City / Forest State wordmark is added in code.
- Fictional characters only: no real people, and no real brand logos (LTC, Western crest, store signs).
- Save each panel separately as PNG, about 1024 px. Keep the same style line on every prompt so the panels match.

## Style line (paste at the start of every panel prompt)
> Bold comic-book illustration, thick clean ink outlines, cel shading, saturated sunset palette of hot pink, orange, gold,
> purple and teal, dramatic low angle, cinematic lighting, grainy print texture, no text, no logos.

## Panels (pick 6–8)
1. **The Goose**: a Canada goose crime boss in a black fedora with a pink band, aviator sunglasses and a gold chain, looking down at the viewer.
2. **Blackfriars Bridge**: the white iron bowstring truss bridge over a river at sunset, a cyclist crossing, low angle.
3. **The clock tower**: a sandstone collegiate-gothic tower with a green copper spire and a glowing clock face at dusk, students below.
4. **The hero**: a university student in a purple hoodie (no crest) sprinting up a grassy hill holding a phone that glows with a map.
5. **City bus**: a green-and-yellow city bus (no logos) racing through a downtown street at night, motion blur, neon reflections.
6. **Covent Garden**: a busy indoor food market, a vendor tossing an apple, warm light.
7. **The Forks**: two friends in a canoe where two rivers meet, a modern museum building and a castle-like brick courthouse behind them.
8. **Haunted theatre**: a ghostly 1900s theatre owner in a top hat in a red velvet balcony box, a marquee glow.
9. **Goose attack**: an angry Canada goose spreading its wings at a startled student on a campus path, comedic.
10. **Richmond Row at night**: neon storefronts, students on scooters, light snow.

## Full collage (optional, one image)
> [style line] A single poster made of 9 angled comic panels separated by thick black gutters, arranged like a classic
> video game cover, with an empty rectangular space in the centre for a title. Panels: [list 8 of the subjects above].
> Portrait 9:16, no text.

## App icon
> [style line] A square app icon: one comic panel with a thick black border, a fierce mustang horse head in profile
> breaking out of the panel, a striped sunset disc behind it, tiny pine silhouettes at the bottom, bold and simple
> enough to read at 60 px, no text.

Alternative icon subject: The Goose's head in fedora and aviators.

Export 1024×1024 PNG, no transparency, with the main subject inside the centre 80% (iOS and Android crop the edges).
I'll make the 180, 192 and 512 px versions and the maskable variant.

## Where to generate (Nov 2026)
- **Gemini app or Google AI Studio (Nano Banana image model):** recommended. Free to start, strong at keeping one
  style across many panels, and it fits the Gemini sponsor-prize story.
- **Midjourney:** the best look for stylised comic illustration, but paid. Use `--ar 1:1` for panels and `--ar 9:16` for the collage.
- **Adobe Firefly:** the safest licensing (trained on licensed content) if commercial use matters later.
- **ChatGPT image generation:** good at following long prompts and making edits one panel at a time.
- Whichever you use, check its terms allow public and commercial use, and note the tool and prompts in this file.

## Handing over
Drop the PNGs in chat (or commit them to `public/cover/`). I'll handle the angled frames, colour grading, panel
animation, wordmark, intro integration, Devpost thumbnail and icon sizes.

content.text:
I made two versions of the cover, both rendered and above:

- **[cover.webp](public/cover/cover.webp)** is a 1080×1920 portrait collage. Because it's named `cover.*`, the loading and title screen will show it automatically in place of the postcard renders, with a slow push-in.
- **[devpost.png](public/cover/devpost.png)** is a 1500×1000 landscape version for your Devpost thumbnail and gallery.

**Layout:** angled panels with thick black gutters, and your Mustang City logo in the centre band with "Graduate knowing your city" under it. I didn't use the two game covers you pasted. They were only inspiration for the layout.

**Panels:** Delilah's, the gas station and the bus, plus two of your own 3D campus renders (the campus overview and University College) to fill the gaps. I trimmed the cream border off the Delilah's and gas-station art, and blended the logo's near-black background into the gutters so no square edge shows.

**Adding panels:** [scripts/build-cover.mjs](scripts/build-cover.mjs) builds both images, and your source art is in `scripts/cover/`. When you have more panels, put them there, add them to the `IMG` list and panel shapes in the script, and run:

```powershell
node scripts/build-cover.mjs
```

**Branding:** two panels show real brands. The bus has London Transit's livery and logo, and the gas station's stripes look like 7-Eleven. Your COVER_ART.md says to avoid real brand logos. That's probably fine for a hackathon, but for the public Devpost image you could swap those panels when you have replacements.

content.text:
Sounds good, I'll leave the logos as they are. Your current panels all share the same look: a comic-ink sunset or night scene of a real London spot. These ideas keep that look but add what the cover is missing so far: **people, action, landmarks and a character**.

**Characters (you need at least one; real game covers are built around faces)**
1. **The Goose boss.** Your quest-giver in a fedora, aviators and a gold chain, looking down at the camera. This is the strongest panel you could add.
2. **The hero.** A student in a purple hoodie running across campus, holding a phone that glows with the fog map.
3. **The crew.** Three students mid-heist outside a building at night, one pointing, one on lookout. This sells the social side.

**Landmarks (these say "London" at a glance)**

4. **UC Hill clock tower** at golden hour, with students sprawled on the grass below.

5. **Blackfriars Bridge**, the white iron truss bridge, with a cyclist crossing at sunset.

6. **Banting House** at dusk with a glowing window. It ties straight into your insulin mission.

7. **The Forks of the Thames**, with friends in a canoe where the two rivers meet.

8. **Covent Garden Market** inside, with warm light and a vendor tossing an apple.

**Action (covers need motion to feel like a game)**

9. **A goose attack.** An angry Canada goose, wings spread, charging a terrified student on a campus path. It's funny and every Western student will recognize it.

10. **Richmond Row at night** in light snow, with neon storefronts and students on scooters.

11. **TD Stadium on game day**, with a crowd in purple, fireworks and a football mid-air.

12. **Someone running to catch the bus** in the snow, with the bus pulling away. This pairs well with your bus panel.

**Vibe and texture**

13. **A late-night food spot**, like a shawarma or pizza place glowing at 2 a.m. with a line outside.

14. **A phone close-up.** A hand holding a phone showing the fog map with "MISSION PASSED" on screen. Your app becomes part of the art.

15. **Springbank Park** at dusk, with fireflies and someone on a bike path.

**Tips so the panels match**
- Start every prompt with the same style line: *bold comic-book illustration, thick ink outlines, cel shading, hot pink / orange / gold / purple / teal sunset palette, dramatic low angle, grainy print texture.*
- **Mix shot types.** Your current panels are all wide building shots. Real covers mix 1–2 close-up faces, a couple of action shots and some wide scenes. The Goose and the goose attack would add the most.
- **Keep the main subject centred.** Panels get cropped into angled shapes, so leave some room around the edges.
- **Ask for no frame.** Request no border, or the art comes back with a cream frame like Delilah's had.

My pick for the next three: **the Goose boss, the goose attack and the UC Hill clock tower.** Send them over and I'll add them to the collage.

content.text:
Here are both prompts. They start with the same style line as your other panels so everything matches.

---

## Logo prompt

> Bold comic-book illustration style, thick clean ink outlines, cel shading, grainy print texture. A logo emblem for a video game called "MUSTANG CITY": a fierce wild mustang horse rearing up on its hind legs, mane and tail whipping like flames, coloured with a sunset gradient of hot pink, orange and gold with purple shadows and small teal highlights. Below the horse, the words "MUSTANG CITY" in a chunky, custom, slightly rounded hand-drawn display lettering stacked on two lines, filled with a pink-to-orange gradient, with a thick cream outline and a heavy black drop shadow. The horse slightly overlaps the top of the lettering. Centred, symmetrical composition, solid pure black background (#000000), no other text, no border, no frame, no tagline. Square 1:1, 1024×1024.

**Tips**
- **Font:** your current wordmark's lettering looks very close to the font on the GTA covers. Your own rules (CLAUDE.md and COVER_ART.md) say no GTA typeface, which is why the prompt asks for *custom* lettering. Keep regenerating until it looks clearly different.
- **Background:** keep it **pure black**. The cover script fades out the logo's dark background, so it blends into the gutters.
- **Spelling:** if the AI misspells the words, generate the horse alone (add "no text") and I can set the wordmark in code.

---

## Middlesex College panel prompt

> Bold comic-book illustration, thick clean ink outlines, cel shading, saturated sunset palette of hot pink, orange, gold, purple and teal, dramatic low angle, cinematic lighting, grainy print texture, no text, no logos. A dramatic low-angle view looking up at a historic university building made of pale grey-tan stone: a long, symmetrical three-storey collegiate-gothic façade with rows of tall narrow windows, and rising from its centre a tall square stone clock tower topped by a pointed green copper spire. The large clock face on the tower glows warm gold. The sky behind is a blazing pink-and-orange sunset with purple clouds, and the first stars are appearing. In the foreground, a wide green lawn with a few students walking with backpacks and phones, long shadows stretching toward the viewer, and autumn trees in orange and red framing both sides. Lit windows glow amber. Epic, heroic, slightly exaggerated perspective, like a video game establishing shot. Square 1:1, 1024×1024, no border, no frame.

**Tips**
- **Accuracy:** attach a real photo of Middlesex College as a reference image if the tool allows it. The tower's proportions and the green spire are what make it recognizable, and AI usually gets them wrong from text alone.
- **Variations:** for a night version, swap the sky for "deep purple night sky, neon pink rim light on the stone, glowing windows". For more action, add "a student sprinting across the lawn toward the tower, holding a glowing phone".
- **Framing:** keep the tower centred with some sky above it, since the panels get cropped into angled shapes.

When you have them, drop them in here and I'll swap in the new logo and add Middlesex to the collage.

content.text:
Got it, you mean the home-screen app icon and the browser tab icon. Your app makes **both from a single file**: save it as `public/brand/icon.png` (1024×1024) and every size is generated at build time, including the 64px tab icon and the 180, 192 and 512px home-screen icons. Until that file exists, the app uses the code-drawn emblem.

An icon has to read at tiny sizes, so **leave out the words**. A full logo with "MUSTANG CITY" turns into mush at tab size.

---

## App icon prompt (recommended)

> Bold comic-book illustration, thick clean ink outlines, cel shading, grainy print texture. A square app icon: a fierce mustang horse head in side profile facing right, mane flowing back like flames, coloured with a hot pink to orange to gold gradient with deep purple shadows and a small teal highlight in the eye. Behind the head, a large glowing sunset disc with horizontal stripes in pink, orange and gold. Solid deep night-purple background (#140A2E). Simple, bold, high contrast, very few details, must be instantly readable at 32 pixels. The horse head fills the centre 70% of the square with even padding around it. No text, no letters, no border, no frame, no rounded corners, no transparency. Square 1:1, 1024×1024.

## Alternative: The Goose

> Same style line as above. A square app icon of a Canada goose head in a black fedora with a hot pink band and gold aviator sunglasses, three-quarter view, smug expression, in front of a striped pink-orange-gold sunset disc on a solid deep purple background (#140A2E). Simple, bold, high contrast, readable at 32 pixels, centred in the middle 70%, no text, no border, no rounded corners, no transparency. Square 1:1, 1024×1024.

The goose is more memorable and funny, while the horse matches your logo better. I'd go with the **horse** for the icon and keep the goose as the character on the cover.

---

**Tips**
- **No rounded corners or transparency.** iOS rounds the corners itself, and a transparent icon shows up with a black background.
- **Leave padding around the subject.** Android crops icons into circles, so keep everything important inside the middle 70–80%.
- **Test it small.** Shrink the result to thumbnail size on your screen. If you can't tell it's a horse, regenerate with "even simpler, fewer lines".
- **Save as `public/brand/icon.png`** and run `npm run build`. The new icons will show up on your next deploy. On your iPhone, delete the old home-screen icon and re-add it, because iOS caches the old one.

## Response Helpers

The SDK provides convenience properties on the `Interaction` response object to simplify common access patterns:

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `output_text` | `string \| null` | The last consecutive run of text from the trailing `model_output` steps. Returns the combined text when the model's final output contains multiple text parts. |
| `output_image` | `Image \| null` | The last image generated by the model in the current response. Returns an object with `data` (base64) and `mime_type`. |
| `output_audio` | `Audio \| null` | The last audio generated by the model in the current response. Returns an object with `data` (base64) and `mime_type`. |

## Stateful Conversation

### Python
```python
interaction1 = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input="Hi, my name is Phil."
)
# Second turn — server remembers context
interaction2 = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input="What is my name?",
    previous_interaction_id=interaction1.id
)
print(interaction2.output_text)
```

```typescript
    input: "What is my name?",
    previous_interaction_id: interaction1.id,
});

```

## Deep Research Agent

Use `deep-research-preview-04-2026` for fast research or `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` for maximum exhaustiveness. Agents require `v1beta` and `background=True`.

### Python
```python
import time
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"})

interaction = client.interactions.create(
    agent="deep-research-preview-04-2026",
    input="Research the history of Google TPUs.",
    background=True
)
while True:
    interaction = client.interactions.get(interaction.id)
    if interaction.status == "completed":
        print(interaction.output_text)
        break
    elif interaction.status == "failed":
        print(f"Failed: {interaction.error}")
        break
    time.sleep(10)
```

```typescript
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiVersion: "v1beta" });

// Start background research
const initialInteraction = await client.interactions.create({
    agent: "deep-research-preview-04-2026",

    background: true,
});

// Poll for results
while (true) {
    const interaction = await client.interactions.get(initialInteraction.id);

    } else if (["failed", "cancelled"].includes(interaction.status)) {
```

## Managed Agents

Managed agents run inside a sandboxed Linux environment hosted by Google (`v1beta`). Fetch the [Managed Agents Quickstart](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/managed-agents-quickstart.md) before writing agent code.

### Antigravity Agent

The Antigravity agent (`antigravity-preview-09-2026`) is the general-purpose managed agent. It can execute code (Bash, Python, Node.js), manage files, browse the web, and use Google Search. It uses `gemini-4-hydrogen` by default and also supports `gemini-4-neon` and `gemini-4-carbon` via `agent_config={"type": "antigravity", "model": "gemini-4-neon"}` (or `"gemini-4-carbon"`). See [Antigravity Agent docs](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/antigravity-agent.md) for capabilities, tools, multimodal input, and pricing.

#### Python
```python
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"})

interaction = client.interactions.create(
    agent="antigravity-preview-09-2026",
    input="Write a Python script that generates the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and saves them to fibonacci.txt. Then read the file and print its contents.",
    environment="remote",
)

print(f"Environment ID: {interaction.environment_id}")
print(interaction.output_text)
```

## Streaming

Set `stream=True` to receive incremental server-sent events. Each stream follows: `interaction.created` → (`step.start` → `step.delta`(s) → `step.stop`)+ → `interaction.completed`.

### Python
```python
for event in client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input="Explain quantum entanglement in simple terms.",
    stream=True,
):
    if event.event_type == "step.delta":
        if event.delta.type == "text":
            print(event.delta.text, end="", flush=True)
    elif event.event_type == "interaction.completed":
        print(f"\n\nTotal Tokens: {event.interaction.usage.total_tokens}")
```

### JavaScript/TypeScript

```typescript
const stream = await client.interactions.create({
    model: "gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input: "Explain quantum entanglement in simple terms.",
    stream: true,
});

    if (event.event_type === "step.delta") {
        if (event.delta.type === "text") {
            process.stdout.write(event.delta.text);
        }
    } else if (event.event_type === "interaction.completed") {
        console.log(`\n\nTotal Tokens: ${event.interaction?.usage?.total_tokens}`);
    }
}
```

Evaluates 1 to 1,000 independent questions (`noul` yes/no, `choice` single-select, `score` ordered rubric) over shared input (text, image, audio, video, PDF) in one pass with `gemini-decision-1`, returning calibrated probabilities, `confidence`, and 0 output tokens. client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"})

```python
result = client.decisions.create(
    model="gemini-decision-1",

```

## Data Model

An `Interaction` response contains `steps`, an array of typed step objects representing a structured timeline of the interaction turn.

### Step Types

**User steps:**
- `user_input`: User input (text, audio, multimodal). Contains `content` array.

**Model/server steps:**
- `model_output`: Final model generation. Contains `content` array with `text`, `image`, `audio`, etc.
- `thought`: Model reasoning/Chain of Thought. Has `signature` field (required) and optional `summary`.
- `function_call`: Tool call request (`id`, `name`, `arguments`).
- `function_result`: Tool result you send back (`call_id`, `name`, `result`).
- `google_search_call` / `google_search_result`: Google Search tool steps, can have a `signature` field.
- `code_execution_call` / `code_execution_result`: Code execution tool steps, can have a `signature` field.
- `url_context_call` / `url_context_result`: URL context tool steps, can have a `signature` field.
- `mcp_server_tool_call` / `mcp_server_tool_result`: Remote MCP tool steps.
- `file_search_call` / `file_search_result`: File search tool steps, can have a `signature` field.

### Content types (inside `content` array on `model_output` and `user_input` steps)
- `text`: Text content (`text` field, plus optional `annotations` such as `{"type": "speech_metadata", "speaker": "...", "style": "..."}` for TTS)
- `image` / `audio` / `document` / `video`: Content with `data`, `mime_type`, or `uri`

### Streaming Event Types

| Event | Description |
|---|---|
| `interaction.created` | Interaction created; includes metadata. |
| `interaction.status_update` | Interaction-level status change. |
| `step.start` | A new step begins. Contains step `type` and initial metadata. |
| `step.delta` | Incremental data for the current step. Contains a typed `delta` object. |
| `step.stop` | The step is complete. Contains `index`. |
| `interaction.completed` | Interaction finished. Contains final `usage`. |

### Delta Types

| Delta Type | Parent Step | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `model_output` | Incremental text token. |
| `audio` | `model_output` | audio chunk (base64). |
| `image` | `model_output` | image chunk (base64). |
| `thought_summary` | `thought` | thinking summary text. |
| `thought_signature` | `thought` | Opaque signature for thought verification. |

**Status values:** `completed`, `in_progress`, `queued`, `requires_action`, `incomplete`, `failed`, `cancelled`

## Gemini Live API

For real-time, bidirectional audio/video/text streaming with the Gemini Live API (`gemini-3.8-live`, `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`, and `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live`), install the **`google-gemini/gemini-live-api-dev`** skill. It covers WebSocket streaming, voice activity detection, background reasoning (extended thinking), asynchronous function calling, session management, ephemeral tokens, and more.

content.text:
**Yes, the key works.** At first the app still couldn't use it, for two reasons in its own code. I fixed both, and all three Gemini features now work on your local dev server.

**What was wrong**
1. **Wrong API version.** Your Gemini library now uses the stable `v1` API by default, but the app formats its requests for `v1beta`. Every call failed with an error, and the app quietly showed the stored text instead. I pinned the client to `v1beta` in [lib/gemini.ts](lib/gemini.ts).
2. **The model is overloaded.** `gemini-4-hydrogen` kept returning "high demand" errors, and one reply took 20 seconds. The app gives up after 5 seconds, so it would have failed during your demo. I switched the default to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, which answers in about 1 second. To switch back, set `GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-4-hydrogen`.

**Test results after the fixes**
- **Goose briefings:** Banting House came back as "...Pay your respects and bring me proof, or else. Honk." (`source: gemini`).
- **Forest FM radio:** Gemini wrote the script, and Gemini TTS returned real audio.
- **Photo check:** I sent a bus image and got pass with confidence 1.0, in 1.3 seconds.

**For the live site:** I only put the key in `.env.local`, which git ignores, so it's local only. Add `GEMINI_API_KEY` in **Vercel → Project → Settings → Environment Variables**, then redeploy. Vercel also needs the code fix, so the deployed app won't use Gemini until it's pushed.

**About the key itself:** you pasted it in chat, and Entire pushes session checkpoints to your GitHub repo. That means this key will probably end up in your repo's checkpoint history on the next push. After judging, delete it in Google AI Studio and make a new one. If the repo is public, do that sooner.

-- Mustang City schema (Tiger Data: Postgres + TimescaleDB). Idempotent: safe to re-run.
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;

DO $$ BEGIN
  CREATE TYPE mission_type AS ENUM ('photo', 'checkin', 'bus', 'heist');
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS district_control (
  neighbourhood_id  integer PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES neighbourhoods(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  faculty           text NOT NULL,
  rep_total         integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  updated_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Continuous aggregate: which cells each user pinged per day.
-- Explored count = SELECT count(DISTINCT h3_cell) FROM user_daily_cells WHERE user_id = $1;
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS user_daily_cells
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 day', ts) AS bucket,
       user_id,
       h3_cell,
       count(*) AS pings
FROM location_pings
GROUP BY bucket, user_id, h3_cell
WITH NO DATA;

SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('user_daily_cells',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '30 days',
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 minute',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '15 minutes',
  if_not_exists => TRUE);

| # | Service | Get it | Env vars | Unlocks | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Gemini API** | Google AI Studio → Get API key | `GEMINI_API_KEY` (optional `RADIO_VOICE`) | Photo mission checks, Goose briefings, Forest FM script + voice, tag and student-job screening, timetable screenshots; can also generate the cover art | Free tier |
| 2 | **Auth0** | auth0.com → free tenant → Regular Web App; follow the README "Auth0" steps (callback URLs + the @uwo.ca Action) | `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH0_SECRET` (`openssl rand -hex 32`), `APP_BASE_URL` | Sign-in, friends, leaderboards, server tags, heists, turf, student jobs | Free |
| 3 | **Tiger Data** (Postgres + TimescaleDB) | tigerdata.com → free trial service → connection string | `DATABASE_URL`, then `npm run db:schema && npm run db:seed` | All account data; GPS pings hypertable; continuous aggregate for weekly stats | Free trial |
| 4 | **Mapbox** | done | `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` | Map | Free tier |

**Why Tiger Data stays the main database (not Supabase):** the schema uses a TimescaleDB hypertable and a continuous
aggregate, it's an MLH prize track the brief prioritises, and Supabase has removed TimescaleDB from its Postgres 17 builds.
Switching fully to Supabase is possible (the app talks plain Postgres via `DATABASE_URL`) but means rewriting those two
features and giving up the Tiger Data prize.

## Recommended add-on: Supabase (Realtime + Storage)

Use Supabase *alongside* Tiger Data for the two things it's best at:
- **Realtime channels:** heist crews update instantly (instead of 5-second polling), the live big-screen `/stage` mirror,
  and future loot challenges.
- **Storage:** real photo files for tags, mission photos and posters (today they're small data URLs).

Get it: supabase.com → new project → Project Settings → API.

Env vars:
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`: public by design and safe with row-level security, but it's a second public key, so
  the constitution's "only the Mapbox token is public" rule needs a one-line amendment. The alternative is relaying
  Realtime through our server.
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`: server only.

Free tier.

## Prize-track extras

content.text:
Everything you asked for this round is in except the two new images. I checked each change in the browser and the production build passes. Nothing is committed yet.

## Prize strategy
**Enter these 7:** First/Second/Third Overall, **Most Adventurous**, **Best Health Hack by Sun Life**, **[MLH] Gemini**, **[MLH] Auth0**, **[MLH] Entire** and **[MLH] GoDaddy domain**.

| Track | Why it's worth it |
|---|---|
| Most Adventurous | Its brief is "a hack that enables others to discover the unknown", which is your pitch almost word for word. Best odds. |
| Sun Life Health | Walking plus meeting people. The new Health card gives you something concrete to demo. |
| Gemini | Now actually working: briefings, radio script and voice, and photo checks. |
| Auth0 | Only @uwo.ca accounts can sign in. Make sure the Auth0 Action is turned on. |
| Entire | Sessions are already on. Mention the checkpoints and the automatic secret redaction in your write-up. |
| GoDaddy | About 15 minutes: claim a domain through MLH's offer and point it at Vercel. |

**Skip:** Tiger Data (dropped, as you said), QNX, PCBWay and Solana (hardware or crypto), Vultr (nothing runs on it), and Canada Life and TinyFish (too much of a stretch). If the rules cap how many prizes you can enter, keep **Most Adventurous, Sun Life and Gemini**.

**For the Sun Life pitch:** students walk more, get outside and meet people through heists and crews, all measured against the WHO 150-minute weekly activity goal. Show the Health card.

## What I built
- **Supabase:** removed the TimescaleDB-only parts from the schema. GPS pings are now a plain indexed table, and the daily-cells summary is a plain view. The app automatically adjusts for Supabase's pooled connection. I updated all the docs that mentioned Tiger Data.
- **Health card** (Profile): active minutes against the WHO 150-minute weekly goal with a progress bar, a walking streak, km, about how many steps, and new places. It only counts real walks.
- **Cover intro:** opens on a close-up of the Goose, pulls back to the full collage, then on tap dives into the Mustang City logo and goes straight into the map flight. It waits for the image to load first.
- **"Tap anywhere to start":** the whole screen is the button now. It says "Tap" on phones and "Click" on laptops, in chunky Bowlby One with a black outline and a slow pulse. I didn't use the actual GTA font (Pricedown) because your own IP rules ban it.
- **Map:** I zoomed out fully, tilted and turned 360° to look:

content.text:
## Your images
Both were right, but you'd saved them at the project root, so I moved them into `scripts/cover/`.
- **Middlesex College** is now the top-right panel.
- **The new logo** already has a transparent background, so no cleanup was needed. I trimmed it, and it now takes up less room on the cover. I also moved the intro dive's target to land on it.

The cover and Devpost image are rebuilt and the build passes. I haven't committed or pushed this yet.

## Your live site
**https://www.mustangcity.rodeo** is up. The bare `mustangcity.rodeo` redirects there, so that's the address to use everywhere. Right now Vercel only has the Mapbox token:
- Briefings show stored text instead of Gemini.
- There's no database, so accounts, tags and turf don't work.
- Auth0 sign-in returns 404.

## Adding the keys to Vercel
I wrote every value for you into **`.env.vercel`** at the project root. Git ignores it, so it won't be committed.
1. Open `.env.vercel` and copy everything in it.
2. Go to **vercel.com**, open your project, then **Settings → Environment Variables**.
3. Click into the **Key** field of a new variable and paste. Vercel splits a pasted `.env` file into separate rows automatically.
4. Leave **Production, Preview and Development** all ticked, then click **Save**.
5. Go to **Deployments**, open the **⋯** menu on the latest deployment, and choose **Redeploy**. Env changes only apply after a redeploy.

The file sets `APP_BASE_URL=https://www.mustangcity.rodeo`. That means two more things need the domain:
- **Auth0 dashboard → Applications → your app → Settings:**
  - Allowed Callback URLs: add `https://www.mustangcity.rodeo/auth/callback`
  - Allowed Logout URLs and Allowed Web Origins: add `https://www.mustangcity.rodeo`
- **Mapbox token:** if it has URL restrictions, add `https://www.mustangcity.rodeo`, or the map will be blank on the live site.

## The Supabase keys you pasted
I saved them in `.env.local`, but the app can't use them. They're for the `supabase-js` client, and the app talks to Postgres directly. It needs a **connection string** that includes your database password:
1. In Supabase, click **Connect** at the top of the project.
2. Choose **Transaction pooler** (port **6543**) and copy the URI.
3. Replace `[YOUR-PASSWORD]` with your database password. If you've forgotten it, reset it under **Project Settings → Database**.
4. Paste it in chat. Then I'll set up the tables, seed the missions, and add it to `.env.vercel`.

You don't need to install `@supabase/server`.

## Vultr: two options that actually make sense
1. **Photo storage on Vultr Object Storage** (~45 min of my time).
   - Mission and tag photos currently live in the database as small text-encoded images. They'd move to a real bucket, which is faster and keeps full-quality photos for Wrapped.
   - It's easy to explain to judges.
   - From you: a Vultr account, an Object Storage bucket, and its access and secret keys.
2. **Live bus relay on a small Vultr server in Toronto** (~1 hour).
   - LTC's live bus feed rejects secure connections from cloud hosts, which is why the app currently falls back to an unencrypted connection. A Vultr server would fetch the feed every few seconds and serve the app a fast, cached copy.
   - It solves a real reliability problem, so it's the better story for judges.
   - From you: a Vultr account and a small server (the free credits cover it), plus SSH access.

You'll need to create the Vultr account yourself, since I can't create accounts. **I'd pick photo storage:** fewer moving parts on demo day, and nothing to babysit.

content.text:
## Fixing the Vercel error
The error means those 6 variables already exist, so Vercel won't import over them. The live site is running the latest code but still acts as if Gemini and Auth0 aren't set up. So the existing values are probably wrong, or they were added after the last deploy. Easiest fix:

1. In Vercel, go to **Settings → Environment Variables**.
2. **Delete** these 6: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH0_SECRET` and `APP_BASE_URL`. Use the **⋯** menu on each row, then **Remove**.
3. Paste the contents of `.env.vercel` into the Key field again and **Save**. This time nothing conflicts.
4. Go to **Deployments**, open **⋯** on the latest one, and click **Redeploy**. This step matters: variables only apply to new deployments.

If you'd rather keep the rows, use **⋯ → Edit** on each one and paste in the value from `.env.vercel`. Make sure `APP_BASE_URL` is exactly `https://www.mustangcity.rodeo`.

Once the redeploy finishes, tell me and I'll check that Gemini and sign-in are live.

## The map now stays on Forest State
- **What I changed:** I clamped the camera to the island itself. Before, you could drift about 40 km out to sea in every direction. Now the furthest you can push puts the island's edge just past the middle of the screen, like a pause-menu map.
- **How I checked:** I tried to fling the camera far past each side, and it stopped at the coastline every time.
- **Still in place:** the zoom-out limit and the tilt cap from earlier.

## More places Vultr could fit
| Idea | What it does | Effort | My take |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Object Storage for photos** | Mission and tag photos stored as real files in a Vultr bucket | ~45 min | Best mix of safe and useful |
| **Serverless Inference as a Gemini backup** | When Gemini returns "high demand" (as it did last night), briefings and radio scripts fall back to an open model on Vultr | ~40 min | Great story: it fixes a real failure you actually hit |
| **Live bus relay on a Toronto server** | A small server fetches LTC's live feed, which rejects connections from cloud hosts, and serves the app a cached copy | ~1 hr | Strong story, but one more thing to keep running |
| **Managed Postgres instead of Supabase** | Same database setup, hosted on Vultr | ~10 min | Easiest win if you haven't built anything on Supabase yet |
| **CDN for the 3D campus models** | Serves the `.glb` model files from Vultr | ~30 min | Weak, since Vercel already does this |

**My pick:** Object Storage plus the Gemini backup. Two clear uses make a stronger entry than one, and neither adds anything to babysit on demo day.

Either way you'll need to create a Vultr account and claim the free credits yourself. Tell me which of these you want, and I'll list exactly which keys to grab.

content.text:
## Did the Vercel env work? Mostly yes
I tested the live site at **www.mustangcity.rodeo**:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Gemini briefings | ✅ Working. Banting House comes back in the Goose's voice ("...bring proof, see?") |
| Forest FM radio | ✅ The script is written by Gemini |
| Auth0 sign-in | ⚠️ Sends you to Auth0, but Auth0 shows **"Callback URL mismatch"** |
| Database | ⏳ Not connected yet, until you send the Supabase connection string |

**To fix sign-in:** in the Auth0 dashboard, open **Applications → Applications → your app → Settings**, then:
- **Allowed Callback URLs:** add `https://www.mustangcity.rodeo/auth/callback`
- **Allowed Logout URLs** and **Allowed Web Origins:** add `https://www.mustangcity.rodeo`
- Click **Save Changes** at the bottom. No redeploy is needed.

## What's new on the title screen
**The cover:**
- **It never sits still.** After the pull-back it slowly "breathes" around the logo.
- **Logo glint:** a light sweep runs across the Mustang City logo every few seconds, and it only lights the logo itself.
- **Poster finish:** a subtle print grain and a dark vignette, so it looks like a printed cover instead of a flat image.

**Pressing start:**
- **LOADING state:** while the map loads you see "LOADING..." in the same chunky lettering, with a sunset progress bar.
- **Press any key:** laptops show "Press any key to start" and any key works (except D, which opens your demo panel). Phones show "Tap anywhere to start".
- **Confirm effect:** when you press, the prompt blinks like an arcade game, with a little two-note blip.
- **The dive:** a rising whoosh plays as the camera dives into the logo, it ends in a white flash, and the flash fades straight into the "Welcome to Forest State" map flight.
- **Credits:** a small "Hack Western 13 · London, ON" line at the bottom.

I watched the whole sequence play in the browser with Enter, Space and a click, and the production build passes.

**Also waiting to be pushed:** the map bounds (no swiping off Forest State) and the new cover with Middlesex and your new logo. I haven't committed or pushed anything yet.

/** The trimmed logo, `h` px tall, centred on (cx, cy). */
async function logo(cx, cy, h) {
  const l = await load(IMG.logo);
  const w = (h * l.width) / l.height;
  return `<image href="${l.uri}" x="${cx - w / 2}" y="${cy - h / 2}" width="${w}" height="${h}"/>`;
}

function tagline(cx, y, size) {
  return `<text x="${cx}" y="${y}" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif" font-weight="900"
    font-size="${size}" letter-spacing="${size * 0.18}" fill="#FFD27A">GRADUATE KNOWING YOUR CITY</text>`;
}

function frame(W, H, body) {
  return `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${W}" height="${H}" viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}">
  <rect width="${W}" height="${H}" fill="${GUTTER}"/>
  ${body}
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="${W}" height="${H}" fill="none" stroke="${GUTTER}" stroke-width="44"/>
</svg>`;
}

// Logo centre is mirrored in components/Intro.tsx (LOGO_ORIGIN) so the intro dive lands on it.
async function portrait() {
  const W = 1080, H = 1920;
  const body = [
    await panel("p1", IMG.gooseBoss, [[0, 0], [560, 0], [520, 700], [0, 730]], [0.4, 0.1]),

content.text:
The animation is fixed, and I checked it by recording it frame by frame rather than by eye.

**What was wrong:**
- **Top-left start:** that was my Goose close-up, and the zoom swung around a fixed corner point, so everything slid diagonally.
- **Easing:** the pull-back front-loaded its movement and then crawled. The dive barely moved and then popped.
- **Stutter risk:** it all ran on the main thread, the same one the map uses while it loads.

**What it does now:**
1. **Opening:** fades up from black centred on the logo, slightly zoomed in, and settles to the full cover in about 1.5 s. No corner pull.
2. **Idle:** slow breathing around the logo, with the softer glint.
3. **On press:**
   - The prompt blinks.
   - The logo punches up.
   - The panels **burst away from the title**: the gas station and Delilah's shoot **straight out sideways**, and the corner panels fly off diagonally.
   - The camera rushes into the **"MUSTANG CITY" lettering**, ending in a white flash into the map flight.
4. **Every refresh** now waits at the title screen for a press, like a console game.

**How I checked:** I logged every panel's position and the camera zoom on each frame. It holds 60 fps (worst frame 25–46 ms), everything fires in order, and the middle panels finish with zero vertical drift. Screenshots confirmed the centred opening.

**How it's built:** the cover script now also exports each panel as its own transparent layer, so the title screen can move them independently. The flat `cover.webp` and `devpost.png` are unchanged for Devpost. Everything runs on the browser's compositor, so map loading can't make it stutter.

**Demo bonus:** your demo panel's "Replay intro" now replays the whole cover sequence from the start.

content.text:
You were right: the game had no loop you could actually finish. Neighbourhoods only unlocked after walking **30% of their area**, which nobody will ever do. Collectibles were invisible until you were within 50 m, and almost every mission was downtown, so most of the city had nothing to do. I built the region-claiming system you described and played it through in the browser.

## How claiming works now
Every one of the **42 neighbourhoods** has a quest board with 4 quests. **Finish 3 and you claim it**: the whole region's fog lifts at once with a crisp border, you get **+150 Rep**, a "REGION CLAIMED" moment plays, and the HUD counter goes up (**Regions 1/42**).

The quests come from **962 real places** I pulled from OpenStreetMap: 67 cafés, 393 food spots, 170 shops, 306 parks and 26 museums.
1. **Set foot:** get there by walking, bike or bus. It ticks off automatically.
2. **Explore:** clear a set number of blocks, about a 20-minute wander. Your existing fog-of-war still counts.
3. **Local stop:** check in at a real café, restaurant or shop. It's GPS-verified, so you have to be within about 45 m, and it lists the nearest options with distances.
4. **Signature:** the region's Goose job or hidden collectible if it has one. Otherwise a named landmark or park, like the Elsie Perrin Williams Estate in Masonville.

## Finding things is easier
- **Missions tab:** now opens with **"Regions near you"**, the closest unclaimed regions with their 4 quest dots and distance (from campus if location is off). Tap one to open its quest board.
- **Profile:** shows all 42 regions, claimed ones first.
- **Collectibles:** they're now signature quests with warmer/colder hints, instead of being invisible.

## Tested end to end
I opened Masonville, then teleported to Big Orange café and checked in. Teleporting there also completed "Set foot" automatically. Then I checked in at the Elsie Perrin Williams Estate, and the region was claimed: Rep went from 106 to 260, the HUD showed 1/42, and the map showed the whole region revealed.

**For your demo:** press **D** to open the demo panel, and every quest gets a **"Go there (demo)"** button. A full region claim takes about 20 seconds on stage.

## The live map error
The production site now has the Mapbox token in its code. The error came from a deploy built while the variable was missing (during the delete and re-import), so a hard refresh should fix it.

## Ideas for next
- **Competition:** region leaderboards against friends and faculties. That needs the Supabase connection string to sync between players.
- **Streaks:** daily quests or streaks so people come back each day.

content.text:
I built both. I checked each one in the browser and the production build passes. Nothing is committed yet.

## Streaks and daily quests
- **3 daily quests,** the same for everyone each day:
  - Two easy ones from: check in somewhere local, explore 10 new blocks, set foot in a new region, finish a Goose job.
  - One **stretch** goal: claim a region, or explore 25 new blocks.
- **Rewards:** each quest is +20 Rep, and finishing all three adds a +50 bonus.
- **Streaks:** do at least one daily a day to keep it going. The streak shows as a **flame next to your rank in the HUD**, and there's a celebration from day 2 onward.
- **Daily card:** it sits at the top of the Missions tab with the streak, today's three quests (with progress bars for the explore ones), and a "New quests in 22h 10m" countdown.
- **Tested:** your Masonville run earlier counted toward today. "Check in somewhere local" and "Claim a region" are done, so you have a 1-day streak and Rep went from 260 to 300.

## Competition
- **Regions leaderboard:** it's now the default ranking on Crew → Leaderboard, filterable by Western, your faculty or your crew, this week or all time. Every row shows the player's streak flame.
- **Faculty war:** each region is held by the faculty with the most members who've claimed it, and faculties are ranked by regions held. Your faculty is highlighted.
- **Server side:** a `region_claims` table, and your claims and streak sync automatically. The leaderboard API ranks by regions and returns the faculty standings.
- **Until Supabase is connected,** it shows the labelled demo crew (Jules 11/42 🔥9, Maya 6/42 🔥4, Dev 2/42) plus you, and a "sample" faculty war. I also fixed a layout bug where the new chips made the sheet scroll sideways.

## To make it live between real players
Send the Supabase **transaction pooler** connection string (port 6543, with your database password). I'll run the database setup, which now includes the new tables, add it to Vercel, and then real Western students rank against each other.
