content.content:
## Queue

- [x] **Mustang City pre-explored with a sharp real campus border + detailed models for every campus building** (Ryan, Nov 21)

- [x] **Replay mode (core #6)** — record the live GPS trace to the device (and `location_pings` when signed in);
  "Replays" list in Profile; play any trace back at 1×/4×/16× so fog clears on screen; demo panel can load
  a bundled sample walk. *Done when:* a recorded 2-minute walk replays at 16× with fog clearing and the
  arrow following; replay never writes new reveals twice.
- [x] **Rank-up toast + badges** — full-screen "RANK UP" moment when rank changes; badge engine for the
  brief's six badges (Cartographer, Goose Whisperer, Night Owl, Heister, Route 6 Regular, Every Route) with a Badges grid
  on Profile; titles selectable under the name. *Done when:* crossing 1,000 Rep (via demo controls) shows the
  toast once; earned badges persist.
- [x] **Neighbourhood unlocks** — London neighbourhood polygons (OSM `place=neighbourhood|suburb` or City of
  London open data, record the source), unlock at 30% of a neighbourhood's cells, +50 Rep, toast, list on
  Profile, large stylised district names at city zoom. *Done when:* demo walk through Old East Village unlocks it.
- [x] **Server ping log** — write live GPS fixes to the `location_pings` hypertable when signed in (batched),
  so replays/Wrapped survive device changes. *Done when:* a signed-in walk appears in `location_pings`; no-op without DB.
- [x] **Leaderboards** — weekly + all-time, filter friends / faculty / all Western, by Rep and % explored
  (continuous aggregate for weekly Rep). *Done when:* two test accounts rank correctly; degrades without DB.
- [x] **Time-of-day palette** — suncalc sunrise/sunset for London drives `lightPreset` (dawn/day/dusk/night),
  re-evaluated every 10 min. *Done when:* forcing the clock to sunset switches to dusk without reload.
- [x] **The Goose quest-giver** — original goose crime-boss portrait (SVG, original art), appears on mission
  briefings; Gemini rewrites briefings in character from stored text (fallback to stored text). *Done when:*
  briefings show the portrait; no facts are added to landmark text.
- [x] **Geo-pinned tags** — leave a note/photo on your current cell; others see it once their fog there is
  cleared; upvotes (+10 Rep). *Done when:* tag created by A appears for B only after B reveals that cell.
- [x] **AI radio host** — tap-to-start radio; Gemini script from current neighbourhood + nearby landmarks,
  Gemini TTS voice; never autoplay. *Done when:* entering a new neighbourhood queues a 15-second segment.
- [x] **Graduation Wrapped** — Spotify-Wrapped-style recap (fog timelapse from replay data, stats,
  percentile), shareable card via Web Share. *Done when:* Wrapped renders from current progress and shares an image.
- [x] **Live buses + route collection** — LTC GTFS static + GTFS-RT in an API route, buses animate on the map,
  mission cards show next arrival; ride detection; "Every Route" progress. *Done when:* live buses move
  (or cached last-good feed with a "delayed" label).
- [x] **Faculty turf + heists** — districts tinted by faculty with most Rep; heist missions needing 3+ players
  within radius/time window. *Done when:* turf colours update from DB; a 3-account heist completes.
- [x] **Polish pack** — poster-style mission cards (canvas + Web Share), hidden collectibles, radar HUD,
  fog decay (6 months), student-written missions with Gemini screening, live weather overlay.
- [x] **Hero 3D model: Middlesex College** (+ University College and 19 campus-core buildings, spec 019) — low-poly glTF via Mapbox `model` layer at z ≥ 16 (see
  `specs/003-friends-buildings/research.md`). *Done when:* model replaces the extrusion, stays at 60 fps.
- [x] **Class Run** — schedule import + class waypoints + on-time Rep (design in `docs/roadmap.md`).

## UI polish plan (documented Nov 21 — queued after Mustang City work; not built yet)
Context: Ryan asked for a super clean, smooth, cohesive UI reminiscent of GTA 6's art direction (postcard art,
sunset palette, full-bleed loading art) without "polygon vibes". Passes 1–2 shipped (design reset, feathered fog,
palette, control stack, building framing, postcard loading screen, unified buttons). Next:

- [x] **Wrapped timelapse art** — replace hard hex cells with soft glowing blobs (smoothed regions + bloom), sunset
  gradient by time; same treatment for the share card.
- [x] **Intro flight + landing polish** — smoother camera curve, captions in the new type style, HUD/tab bar/stack
  stagger in with springs, no pop-in of labels/blips during the dive.
- [x] **3D model day/night look** — window glow keyed to the light preset per material (separate emissive for
  night), softer roof colour by day, subtle ambient occlusion band at the base.
- [x] **Typography pass** (Nov 21: body text on a 12/14/16/20 scale, two letter-spacing tokens, display titles unchanged) — one condensed display face for titles + one UI face; fewer letter-spaced caps labels;
  consistent sizes (12/14/16/20/30).
- [x] **Motion pass** (Nov 21: shared EASE_OUT + SPRING_UI/POP/HERO tokens in lib/motion.ts; MotionConfig reducedMotion="user") — shared easing tokens; spring sheets with velocity; tab-switch cross-fade; reduced-motion audit.
- [x] **Empty/first-run states** (first-run cards done; more empty states welcome) — friendly first-run pointers, empty states with a next action, "Set your name"
  onboarding card.
- [x] **Map legend + blip toggles** — brief §Map; one tidy panel instead of more floating chips.
- [x] **Accessibility audit** (Nov 21: text floor ink/60 = 6.5:1; all controls ≥ 44 pt and named; Dynamic Type still open — px sizes don't scale with iOS text size) — contrast on glass, 44 pt targets, VoiceOver labels for map controls, Dynamic Type.
## 0. Ranked by hackathon win odds (Nov 21)

How judges actually see the project: the Devpost video first, then ~3 minutes of live demo, often holding the phone
themselves. So ranking = (how much a judge notices it in that window) × (how likely it lands) ÷ effort.

| # | Idea | Why it moves the odds | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Devpost trailer** (§1) | Judges watch the video before anything else; intro flight + fog timelapse + MISSION PASSED cut to music | M |
| 2 | **Comic-panel cover art intro** (§8, Ryan) | Sells the genre in the first 5 seconds of both the video and the live demo; cheap if the art is generated | S (+ art) |
| 3 | **Live big-screen mirror `/stage`** (§1) | Fog clearing live on a laptop while you walk up to the judges is the "wow" moment | M |
| 4 | **"Wanted level" for curiosity** (§1) | Instantly reads as the genre, tiny build, shows on every screen | S |
| 5 | **The Goose calls you** (§1) | Character + Gemini TTS = memorable + strengthens the Gemini sponsor prize | M |
| 6 | **First-run coach marks** (§5) | Judges hold the phone cold; 3 pointers stop them getting lost | S |
| 7 | **Stash & carry inventory** (§8, Ryan) | Gives the city a real game loop ("bring it home to Mustang City") — great pitch line; needs a scripted demo beat to show | M |
| 8 | **Pause-screen music** (§4) | Atmosphere makes every demo second feel like a game; procedural version needs no licence | S |
| 9 | **Near-miss nudges** (§2) | "3% from unlocking Old East Village" is a one-line demo of the hook loop | S |
| 10 | **Photo mode** (§1) | Shareable stills for Devpost/socials | S |
| 11 | **Variable rewards on pass** (§2) | Makes the MISSION PASSED beat land harder | S |
| 12 | **Accessibility mode** (§1) | Impact story some judges weigh heavily | M |
| 13 | **O-Week mode** (§1) | Real-user adoption story at Western | S |
| 14 | **Daily Job + forgiving streaks** (§2) | Retention judges ask about; mostly a pitch slide | S |
| 15 | **Radio news interruptions** (§1) | Nice, but needs friends + radio on during the demo | M |
| 16 | **Loot challenges between players** (§8, Ryan) | Exciting, but needs real-time multiplayer, opt-in location and a mini-game — high risk of a broken demo | L |
| 17 | **Heist trailer generator** (§1) | Strong but big; the Devpost trailer covers most of the value | L |
| 18 | Push notifications, seasonal events, collection sets, friend overlap, surprise blips, rank perks (§2) | Long-term retention; little visible in 3 minutes | S–M |
| 19 | **Sustainability stats** (§1) | Only matters for a sustainability track | S |

**Suggested next build order if approved:** 2 → 4 → 6 → 8 → 1 (record the trailer last, once everything looks final) → 3 → 5 → 7.

The `/build-next` skill works through this list **top to bottom, one item per run**. Order follows the
brief's build plan and cut list (core first). Each item has "Done when" checks the agent verifies itself.

Status marks: `[ ]` todo · `[x]` done · `[~]` blocked (reason in the line) · `[>]` in progress

Full list with decisions: [docs/IDEAS.md §7](IDEAS.md#7-needs-from-ryan). Ideas awaiting review live in `docs/IDEAS.md` (not built).
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` — photo checks, goose dialogue, radio host

| ✓ | Idea | Why it wins | Effort | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ ] | **"Wanted level" for curiosity** — 1–5 stars that rise while you're in a fogged area for the first time and fade when you've cleared it; stars glow on the HUD | Instantly reads as the genre to every judge; zero IP (stars are generic) | S | ★★★ |
| [ ] | **Live demo mode on the big screen** — `/stage` route: full-screen map that mirrors your phone's fog in real time while you walk the judging hall | Judges watch fog clear live as you walk up to them | M | ★★★ |

| [ ] | **The Goose calls you** — fake incoming-call screen (original UI) when a new mission unlocks nearby; Gemini TTS voice line | Memorable character moment, uses Gemini TTS | M | ★★★ |
| [ ] | **Faculty war room** — weekly turf map where each faculty's colour floods the districts it leads; Monday "turf report" card | Campus-wide competition → retention + demo beat | M | ★★ |
| [ ] | **Mustang City Radio "news" interruptions** — when a friend unlocks a district, the radio host breaks in with a 5-second bulletin | Ties social + AI + audio together | M | ★★ |
| [ ] | **Photo mode** — hide UI, letterbox, film grain, sunset LUT, date/location stamp; share card | People share screenshots = free marketing | S | ★★ |
| [ ] | **Accessibility pitch** — "explore without walking" mode: wheelchair-accessible routes from City of London open data, fog clears along accessible paths | Strong impact story for judges | M | ★★ |
| [ ] | **Sustainability track** — kilometres walked vs. driven, CO₂ saved, LTC rides counted | Fits sponsor tracks | S | ★ |
| [ ] | **Orientation-week mode** — Western O-Week preset missions (residence → classes → food) for first-years | Real user pull at Western | S | ★★ |
| [ ] | **Devpost assets** — 60-s trailer cut from the intro flight + replay, original synthwave bed, captions | Judges watch the video first | M | ★★★ |

## 2. Keeping players hooked (retention)

| ✓ | Hook | Mechanic | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ ] | **Daily Job** | One rotating Goose mission per day, +2× Rep if done before midnight; streak flame on the HUD | S |
| [ ] | **Streaks with forgiveness** | Walk-streak (any new fog per day); one "safehouse day" freeze per week so streaks don't feel punishing | S |
| [ ] | **Weekly reset leaderboards** | Already have weekly Rep; add Monday push "You finished #4 in Science — 120 Rep behind #3" | S |
| [ ] | **Near-miss nudges** | "You're 3% from unlocking Old East Village" when the app opens; region card shows the closest unexplored street | S |
| [ ] | **Collection sets** | Landmark sets (Bridges, Haunted, Film Sets, Heritage Plaques) with set-completion badges and a profile shelf | M |
| [ ] | **Fog regrowth (opt-in)** | Cells untouched for 6 months slowly re-fog (already in Polish pack) → reason to revisit | M |
| [ ] | **Friend fog overlap** | "You and Maya have both cleared 12% of downtown — 3% overlap" + co-op missions that need both | M |
| [ ] | **Seasonal events** | Homecoming, Halloween (haunted Grand Theatre hunt), Winter "Frost City" palette, Grad Week Wrapped | M |
| [ ] | **Surprise blips** | Random gold blips that exist for 2 hours (location from a seeded daily RNG) worth bonus Rep | S |
| [ ] | **Rank perks** | Each rank unlocks something visible: HUD colours, map filters, emblem, title, radio station | S |
| [ ] | **Push notifications (PWA)** | iOS 16.4+ supports web push for home-screen PWAs: daily job, friend passed you, streak at risk | M |
| [ ] | **Variable rewards on mission pass** | Small chance of a rare "golden photo" frame or bonus Rep roll — the pass screen becomes a slot-machine moment | S |

## 3. Real 3D models of Western's buildings

content.content:
### Stash & carry inventory (Mustang City is your stash)
- **Loop:** loot you pick up out in Forest State (collectibles, mission rewards, rare drops) goes into a **carry bag** with
  limited slots (e.g. 6, +1 per rank). It only becomes permanent once you **bank it at the stash** — any spot inside
  Mustang City (campus geofence), or a stash building like UCC. Full bag → you must go back to campus or drop something.
- **Why it fits:** turns campus into home base (the brief's whole premise), gives every trip out a reason to come back,
  and makes Rep from loot feel earned. Shows well as a HUD bag counter + a "STASHED" moment when you walk onto campus.
- **Build sketch:** `inventory` (carried) and `stash` tables (or device storage first); items = existing collectibles +
  mission drops; bag UI in Profile; geofence check in the location pipeline (same as Class Run arrival).
- **Effort:** M for single-player (no DB needed to demo).

### Losing loot / player challenges (multiplayer)

## Approved Nov 22 — "approve everything" (Ryan, away; build continuously, don't stop to ask)
Built in this order; each item is browser-checked, committed and pushed (secrets scan on Entire checkpoints).
- [>] **UI tweaks** — remove the radar, smaller HUD, remove the Mapbox wordmark + attribution button (credits move to Profile).
- [ ] **Region side quests + map blips** — varied demo "husk" quests for every region (photo op, bus ride in, night visit,
  food crawl, tag, crew check-in…); quest blips on the map that only appear when zoomed in (no clutter at city zoom).
- [ ] **First-run coach marks** (IDEAS §5) — 3 skippable pointers: tap a region, do its quests, check your dailies.
- [ ] **Near-miss nudges** (IDEAS §2) — "1 quest from claiming Masonville" card on the map.

# Devpost copy (paste-ready, no em dashes)

## About the project

```markdown
## Inspiration

Most of us didn't grow up in London. We arrive at 18, live inside a bubble of campus, Richmond Row and one bus route, and four years later most of us leave. We spend four years in a city and never actually meet it.

We already explore cities obsessively, just in games. Open-world games make you *want* to see what's behind the fog. So I asked: what if London was the open world?

## What it does

**Mustang City** is a GTA 6-inspired mobile web app that turns London, Ontario into **Forest State**, an open-world map covered in black fog. Western's campus is your home base, Mustang City, and the rest of the city is waiting to be uncovered.

**Claim all 42 regions.** Walking every street isn't realistic, so each of London's 42 neighbourhoods has a quest board built from real local places: set foot there, explore a few blocks, grab a coffee at a local café, and hit its signature spot. Finish 3 of 4 and the whole region's fog lifts at once. Your headline stat is simply *Regions 3/42*.

**Something to do everywhere.** Every region also has light side quests pinned to real spots: a photo op, riding in on a real LTC bus stop, a night shift, local trivia, a food crawl, a crew meet-up. They appear on the map as you zoom in, so the city view never gets cluttered.

**A reason to open it every day.** Three daily quests and a streak flame, plus three gold *surprise blips* a day that vanish at midnight.

**Beat your friends and your faculty.** A regions leaderboard (this week or all time, all of Western, your faculty or your crew) and a faculty war, where each region is held by the faculty with the most members who claimed it.

**It feels like a game.**
- **The Goose:** an original crime-boss quest-giver who *calls you* when you walk into a new region, voiced with Gemini.
- **MISSION PASSED:** photo missions to real landmarks checked by Gemini, with a chance of a golden 1.5× Rep roll.
- **Stash and carry:** loot drops into a limited bag, and it only counts once you bring it home to Mustang City.
- **Wanted level:** curiosity stars that heat up while you're on an exploring streak.
- **Atmosphere:** an original procedural synthwave soundtrack, a comic-panel title screen that bursts apart into the map, and photo mode for postcards.
- **Live data:** London Transit buses on the map in real time.
- **Graduation Wrapped:** the map of your four years, at the end.

**Graduate knowing your city.**

## How I built it

- **Frontend:** Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind v4 and Motion, as a PWA for the iPhone home screen.
- **Map:** Mapbox GL JS (Standard style). Fog is an H3 hex grid smoothed into one polygon. Claimed regions are unioned into the fog's holes so they lift with a crisp border.
- **Real places:** 962 cafés, shops, parks and landmarks from OpenStreetMap, mapped to the City of London's 42 planning districts to generate every quest board.
- **AI:** the Gemini API handles photo verification, The Goose's dialogue, the radio host and every voice line through Gemini TTS. A strict rule covers all of it: facts come from stored, sourced text, and Gemini restyles them but never adds new ones.
- **Accounts and data:** Auth0 sign-in, with Supabase Postgres for region claims, leaderboards and the faculty war.
- **Live transit:** LTC GTFS and GTFS-Realtime.
- **Title screen:** the comic cover is exported as separate layers and animated on the compositor, so it stays smooth while the map loads.
- **Hosting:** Vercel, at mustangcity.rodeo (GoDaddy Registry).
- **Process:** built solo with AI coding agents, with every session checkpointed through Entire.

## Challenges

- **Making exploration realistic:** nobody walks a whole neighbourhood, which is why regions are claimed through quests at real local spots instead.
- **Custom 3D in Mapbox:** campus models needed non-interleaved buffers, uint16 indices and absolute URLs.
- **Fog that looks good:** raw hexagons look like a spreadsheet. Merging, smoothing and feathering them, plus crisp borders for claimed regions, took several passes.
- **Smooth animation during a heavy map load:** the title animation moved onto the browser compositor.
- **Accuracy vs personality:** The Goose is funny without inventing history, because of the fact guard.
- **Privacy:** there's no live location sharing. Friends see where you've been, never when.

## What I learned

How to bend a map engine into a game engine, how to design a progression loop people can actually finish, how to keep an LLM useful without letting it make things up, and how to scope as a solo builder.

## What's next

Real multiplayer heists, seasonal events (Homecoming, a Halloween hunt), local businesses sponsoring region quests, and photo-real campus facades.
```

## Built with

```
next.js, typescript, react, tailwind-css, motion, mapbox, mapbox-gl-js, h3, openstreetmap, gltf, auth0, supabase, postgresql, gemini, google-gemini, gtfs, gtfs-realtime, open-meteo, web-audio-api, vercel, pwa, node.js, javascript, claude-code, entire
```

## Try it out

- https://www.mustangcity.rodeo
- https://github.com/RyanPeters06/mustang-city
